title: Free Printable Word Searches by Theme, With Answer Keys
metaDescription: Browse free printable word searches for holidays, science, animals, everyday topics and geography, each with a themed word list and an answer key to print.
h1: Free Printable Word Searches by Theme
intro: Each word search page below comes with its own theme word list, a generator that builds a fresh grid and an answer key. Choose a topic, adjust the words if you like, and print as many puzzles as you need.

sections.heading: What you can change on each page
body: The word list, the grid size and the direction of the words are all in your hands. Younger children do best with words that run across and down only, and a small grid. Older students and adults can switch on diagonals and backwards words for a real challenge.
The answer key prints on its own page, so you can keep it back while students solve. Give the puzzle a new title if you want to name a unit, a class or a birthday.
Because the grid is built from a seed, you can share the link to a puzzle and the recipient sees exactly the same one. That makes it easy to hand a puzzle to a co-teacher or a grandparent.

sections.heading: Picking a theme
body: Frog and pond themes are our home territory: try the [frog life cycle](/word-search/frog-life-cycle/) and [pond animals](/word-search/pond-animals/) puzzles for a science lesson that starts with eggs and ends with tadpoles.

Seasonal puzzles such as [Christmas](/word-search/christmas/) and [Halloween](/word-search/halloween/) arrive when you most need them, and subject puzzles on weather, the solar system and the human body support classroom units all year.
If you need something exact, open the [word search maker](/word-search-maker/), paste in your own spelling list, and let it place the words for you. It checks that every word fits before it prints.

faq.q: Do the word searches come with answers?
faq.a: Yes. Turn on the answer key option and it prints on a separate page.

faq.q: What is the best grid size for children?
faq.a: For ages five to seven, a small grid with 8 to 10 short words is plenty. Increase the size as children grow in confidence.
